{{short description|Spanish physicist (1928–2022)}}
'''María Inmaculada Paz-Andrade''' ([[Pontevedra]], 14 November 1928 – Pontevedra, 24 November 2022) was a Spanish physicist and researcher. She was the first person to be named a professor of the Compostela Faculty of Physics, and became an international authority in [[Calorimetry|microcalorimetry]], which is a technique for the measurement of very small quantities of heat.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Falece a catedrática Inmaculada Paz Andrade, honoris causa pola UVigo en 2018 {{!}} Universidade de Vigo |url=https://www.uvigo.gal/universidade/comunicacion/duvi/falece-catedratica-inmaculada-paz-andrade-honoris-causa-uvigo-2018 |access-date=2023-11-08 |website=www.uvigo.gal |language=gl}}</ref>

==Life and work==
Paz-Andrade (sometimes written as Paz Andrade) earned a doctorate in physics (1963) and became a Professor of Applied Physics (specializing in Thermodynamics) and a researcher at the [[University of Santiago de Compostela]]. She also earned a certificate of higher studies at the [[Aix-Marseille University|University of Marseille]] (France). She furthered her studies at the [[University of Manchester]] (UK) (where she was the first woman to be appointed a visiting research professor) and at the Institute of Microcalorimetry and Thermogenesis of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) in Marseille.<ref name=":0" /> 

Having learned about [[Calorimetry|microcalorimetry]] abroad, in 1964 she was the first to teach the subject to researchers in Spain. Specifically, she carried out work on applied [[thermodynamics]], calorimetric studies and determinations of specific heat of solids and liquids.<ref name=":0" /> At the [[University of Santiago de Compostela]], she served as department director of Fundamental Physics at the Faculty of Sciences (1964–1970 and 1972–1974) and then director of the Department of Applied Physics (1986–1992).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2020 |title=PREMIOS MARÍA JOSEFA WONENBURGER PLANELLS |url=https://unidadedamullereciencia.xunta.gal/sites/default/files/2021-01/Folleto%20Wonenburger%202020-WEB_1.pdf |page=4 |language=es}}</ref>

In 1999 she created the multidisciplinary THOR group, to develop computer tools to fight against forest fires in all their stages in [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]] and [[Santiago de Compostela]]. In 1999, more than 40 specialists from different universities were collaborating in the group.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-24 |title=Muere la catedrática Inmaculada Paz Andrade |url=https://www.farodevigo.es/gran-vigo/2022/11/24/fallece-catedratica-inmaculada-paz-andrade-79039595.html |access-date=2023-11-08 |website=Faro de Vigo |language=es}}</ref>

In 2018, Paz-Andrade was awarded an [[Honorary degree|Honorary doctorate]] from the [[University of Vigo]].<ref name=":0" /> 

Paz-Andrade authored more than 200 scientific publications and supervised 39 doctoral theses.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

She was the niece of [[Valentín Paz Andrade|Valentín Paz-Andrade]].

== Honors ==

* Gold Medal of the Royal Spanish Society of Physics (1992)<ref name=":0" />
* Antonio Casares and Rodrigo Galicia Research Award (1999)<ref name=":1" />
* Gold badge of the University of Santiago de Compostela (2000)<ref name=":1" />
* Castelao Medal, awarded by the Government of Galicia (2008).<ref>{{Cite web |title=DOG 116 del 17/06/2008 - DECRETO 118/2008, de 12 de junio, por el que se concede la Medalla Castelao. |url=https://www.xunta.gal/dog/Publicados/2008/20080617/Anuncio2951A_es.html |access-date=2023-11-08 |website=www.xunta.gal}}</ref> 
* Arts. presented in honor of Professor María Inmaculada Paz Andrade. Vol. 26, No. 8 of [[The Journal of Chemical Thermodynamics|Journal of chemical thermodynamics]]. Publisher Academic Press, 911 pp. 1994
* Maria Josefa Wonenburger Planells Prize, awarded by the Government of Galicia (2008).<ref name=":1" />
* Honorary doctorate from the University of Vigo (2018)<ref name=":0" />
